events.title: Danube legions proclaim Septimius Severus emperor
events.description: After the murder of Pertinax, the legions at Carnuntum hailed their governor Septimius Severus as emperor. He marched on Rome, defeated his rivals and founded the Severan dynasty.
events.html: After the murder of Pertinax, the legions at Carnuntum hailed their governor Septimius Severus as emperor. He marched on Rome, defeated his rivals and founded the Severan dynasty.

events.title: Mongols defeat a Polish and German army at Legnica
events.description: A Mongol force under Baidar and Kadan crushed the army of Duke Henry II the Pious, who was killed. Two days later the main Mongol army destroyed the Hungarians at Mohi.
events.html: A Mongol force under Baidar and Kadan crushed the army of Duke Henry II the Pious, who was killed. Two days later the main Mongol army destroyed the Hungarians at Mohi.

events.title: Glarus defeats a Habsburg army at the Battle of Näfels
events.description: The men of Glarus, helped by Schwyz and their allies of the Old Swiss Confederacy, defeated a much larger army of the Habsburg Duchy of Austria. The victory secured the independence of Glarus from Habsburg rule and is commemorated every April.
events.html: The men of Glarus, helped by Schwyz and their allies of the Old Swiss Confederacy, defeated a much larger army of the Habsburg Duchy of Austria. The victory secured the independence of Glarus from Habsburg rule and is commemorated every April.

events.title: The Council of Ferrara opens under Pope Eugene IV
events.description: Pope Eugene IV presided over the first solemn session of the council he had moved from Basel to Ferrara, attended by the Eastern Roman Emperor and the Patriarch of Constantinople. It debated the issues of the East–West Schism.
events.html: Pope Eugene IV presided over the first solemn session of the council he had moved from Basel to Ferrara, attended by the Eastern Roman Emperor and the Patriarch of Constantinople. It debated the issues of the East–West Schism.

events.title: La Salle claims the Mississippi basin for France
events.description: Reaching the mouth of the Mississippi, René-Robert Cavelier de La Salle claimed its whole drainage basin for Louis XIV and named it Louisiana. France sold the territory to the United States in 1803.
events.html: Reaching the mouth of the Mississippi, René-Robert Cavelier de La Salle claimed its whole drainage basin for Louis XIV and named it Louisiana. France sold the territory to the United States in 1803.

events.title: Lee surrenders to Grant at Appomattox Court House
events.description: Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant. Other Confederate forces followed in the weeks after, bringing the American Civil War to an end.
events.html: Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant. Other Confederate forces followed in the weeks after, bringing the American Civil War to an end.

events.title: Germany invades Denmark and Norway
events.description: German forces struck both neutral states in Operation Weserübung. Denmark yielded within hours, while Norway, aided by Britain and France, fought on for two months, giving Germany vital North Sea and Atlantic bases.
events.html: German forces struck both neutral states in Operation Weserübung. Denmark yielded within hours, while Norway, aided by Britain and France, fought on for two months, giving Germany vital North Sea and Atlantic bases.

events.title: Dietrich Bonhoeffer is executed at Flossenbürg
events.description: Lutheran pastor and theologian Dietrich Bonhoeffer was hanged on Hitler's orders for his links to the resistance. He died a month before Germany's surrender.
events.html: Lutheran pastor and theologian Dietrich Bonhoeffer was hanged on Hitler's orders for his links to the resistance. He died a month before Germany's surrender.

events.title: Baghdad falls and Saddam's statue is pulled down
events.description: As US troops entered central Baghdad, a statue of Saddam Hussein in Firdos Square was toppled with the help of a Marine vehicle. The images marked the regime's collapse, though years of insurgency followed.
